text:
Ana: Quick sync — we're losing high-cardinality traces when we fan-out to Tempo+Honeycomb. Tempo sampling/tenant retention differs and traces get split :eyes:
Mike: Yea saw that on prod last week, analysts couldn't join spans because Tempo had a 1% ingested sample while Honeycomb had full. Pain to debug :grimacing:
Sasha: Is this because each exporter applies independent sampling? Our otelcol config currently fans out raw spans to both exporters, then exporters/servers apply their own retention/sampling rules.
Julian: Proposal: add an ingestion-level signal (attribute) 'redwood.retention_ttl' that router/collector uses to choose backend(s) + target tenant. That avoids relying on downstream sampling differences. :+1:
Ana: We should prefer something services can set without SDK churn. Header like `x-redwood-ttl` on our internal HTTP API is easy, but we need a hop to carry it into OTLP payloads.
Mike: Headers won't survive grpc OTLP well. Better to have a small collector processor that maps incoming header -> span/resource attribute so OTLP path carries it consistently.
infra-bot: FYI: OTLP/gRPC supports exporting attributes in the resource & span. See spec: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-proto
Sasha: Config sketch for otelcol to set attribute from env/header and route exporters (very rough):
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      http:
      grpc:
processors:
  attributes/ttl_mapper:
    actions:
      - key: redwood.retention_ttl
        action: insert
        from_attribute: http.request.header.x-redwood-ttl
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [ttl_mapper, routing]
      exporters: [honeycomb, tempo]
extensions: []
```
Julian: Router logic idea: priority rules — if redwood.retention_ttl == "long" -> send to tempo-long-retention tenant and Honeycomb; if "short" -> send only to Honeycomb with TTL tags. Also tag root span with `redwood.routing.sample_decision` to keep sampling decisions consistent.
Mike: Caveat: Tempo's retention is tenant-level; you can't set per-trace TTL in Tempo unless you implement separate tenants or an archive tier. So per-trace TTL mapping requires us to create separate Tempo tenants (or an archive pipeline) and route traces there.
Ana: Right — so implementation plan: (a) collector attribute processor + routing rules (b) create `tempo-archive` tenant for >30d retention (c) ensure billing/ingest controls to avoid surprise costs.
Julian: Action items: Sasha -> PR with otelcol processor config and unit tests; Mike -> router unit/integration tests + dashboard metrics; Julian -> infra work to provision `tempo-archive` tenant and add RBAC. ETA: 2 sprints. Agree?
Sasha: Agree. I'll include an opt-in flag `enable_cross_backend_retention` (default false) so we can test without double-writing for everyone.
Mike: Also add metrics: `router.rewrites`, `router.forwarded_spans`, and a trace-sanity check that flags when same trace id has differing root span counts across backends. I'll wire those into the console dashboard.

Ana: Thanks everyone. I'll update the runbook and ping privacy + billing about tenant creation. Leaving this thread open for PR links. :raised_hands:
